qa_pairs.question: What steps and fees are required to add a course after the standard add/drop period ends?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A late add requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval. The late-add window runs from the end of standard add/drop through the census date.

qa_pairs.question: If I drop a course, how much tuition is reversed depending on when I drop it?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: For a course dropped by the end of standard add/drop, 100% of that course's tuition is reversed. From the day after standard add/drop through the census date, 50% is reversed. After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal.

qa_pairs.question: When does dropping a course record a W grade instead of a simple drop?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Before or on the census date, the portal records a drop. After the census date and through the withdrawal deadline, a course withdrawal receives a W grade. For Fall 2026, the last day to withdraw with a W is October 30.

contexts.text: Before or on census, the portal records a drop. After census and through the withdrawal deadline in `01_academic_calendar.md`, the course receives a `W`.

qa_pairs.expected_answer: To renew, a recipient must complete at least 12 graded Northstar credits in the reviewed term, earn a term GPA of at least 3.30, maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20, and have no active serious-conduct sanction.

qa_pairs.question: How does an approved medical leave affect the Northstar Merit Scholarship?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity. The leave also preserves the student's programme place.

contexts.text: An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity.

qa_pairs.question: Can a parent who pays tuition receive a student's academic or conduct records?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: No. A parent or sponsor who pays tuition does not automatically receive academic or conduct information. The university may discuss a student's record only with the student or a person who has valid, recorded authorization.

contexts.text: The university may discuss a student's record only with the student or a person who has a valid, recorded authorization. A parent or sponsor who pays tuition does not automatically receive academic or conduct information.

qa_pairs.question: A student discussed a late-add request in July 2026 but submits it on August 20, 2026. Which Registration Policy version applies and what fee is charged?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Version 2.0 applies because the late-add request is made on or after August 1, 2026. The late-add fee is USD 40 per course, even if the student first discussed the request in July. A newer publication does not silently rewrite the transaction, but the triggering request date here falls under version 2.0.

contexts.text: Version 2.0, effective August 1, 2026, allows late adds only through census and charges USD 40 per course. A late-add request made on or after August 1, 2026 follows version 2.0 even if the student first discussed the request in July.
The policy in force on the triggering event date controls unless a newer policy explicitly states that it applies retroactively.

qa_pairs.question: A student is on a waitlist for an open course. When a seat opens, what offer is made and which rules can override the waitlist position?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: When a seat opens, the first eligible student receives a 24-hour offer. If the offer expires, the next eligible student is contacted. Waitlist position does not override prerequisite, time-conflict, or hold rules.

contexts.text: When a seat opens, the first eligible student receives a 24-hour offer. If the offer expires, the next eligible student is contacted. Waitlist position does not override prerequisite, time-conflict, or hold rules.

qa_pairs.question: A student has completed all academic requirements for graduation but has an unpaid tuition balance. Can the degree be conferred?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: No. Degree conferral also requires clearance of financial, library, conduct, and document holds. A financial hold does not erase completed academic requirements, but it blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript until the hold is resolved.

contexts.text: Degree conferral also requires clearance of financial, library, conduct, and document holds. A financial hold does not erase completed academic requirements, but it blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript until resolved under `03_tuition_payment_refund.md`.
The hold blocks new registration, official transcripts, and graduation clearance.

qa_pairs.question: What happens if no grade is submitted by the default deadline for an incomplete (I) grade, and what conditions are required to grant an I in the first place?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An I incomplete grade may be granted when at least 70% of assessed work is complete, the student was passing before an unexpected documented event, and the remaining work can be completed independently. If no grade is submitted by the default deadline (the end of the next regular term), the I converts to F unless an approved extension exists.

contexts.text: The default deadline is the end of the next regular term. If no grade is submitted by that deadline, the `I` converts to `F` unless an approved extension exists.

An `I` incomplete grade may be granted when at least 70% of assessed work is complete, the student was passing before an unexpected documented event, and the remaining work can be completed independently.

qa_pairs.question: A student receives an approved medical withdrawal. What tuition relief applies and what must be considered before any refund is calculated?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An approved medical withdrawal may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study, calculated from the last documented date of participation. It is not a cash refund. Scholarship funds are adjusted before any student refund is calculated, so the amount a scholarship student sees first is not final.

contexts.text: An approved medical withdrawal may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study, calculated from the last documented date of participation. It is not a cash refund and requires the process in `06_leave_and_withdrawal.md`.
Scholarship funds are adjusted before any student refund is calculated.

qa_pairs.question: I was told that if I stop attending a course without withdrawing, I will automatically get a refund. Is that right?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: No, that is not correct. A student who stops attending without dropping or withdrawing remains enrolled and may receive a failing grade; stopping attendance is not a withdrawal and tuition is not refunded. The assistant should not confirm the false premise and should state only what the policy documents support.

contexts.text: The assistant must not invent a policy when the documents do not contain an answer. If information is missing or two current documents appear inconsistent, it should say what is known, identify the uncertainty, and direct the student to the responsible office.
A student who stops attending without dropping or withdrawing remains enrolled and may receive a failing grade.
Stopping attendance is not a withdrawal.
